transcript_tail.text: You've hit your org's monthly usage limit

Quick answer first, then I'll check the domain and keep moving.

**SSG = Static Site Generator.** It's a tool that takes your content (markdown/components) plus templates and, at *build time*, spits out plain HTML/CSS/JS files — no server, no database at runtime. Cloudflare Pages just serves those files. Examples: Astro, Eleventy, Hugo, Jekyll. For your 3-page hub, Astro lets the header/footer/architecture-diagram be written once and reused across all three pages, while still outputting pure static files. (The alternative is hand-writing plain HTML — zero build step, but you copy-paste the shared bits.)

Let me check domain availability and my local toolchain in parallel.

No node/npm locally — that settles the SSG question pragmatically: I'll ship **plain HTML** (zero build, no toolchain, deploys to Cloudflare Pages as-is). The domain check was inconclusive (empty result could mean unregistered *or* sandboxed network). Let me confirm via RDAP.

**Domain: `jdtogni.dev` is available** — RDAP returned `404 jdtogni.dev not found`, which means it's unregistered and free to grab at Cloudflare Registrar. And since there's no node/npm on this machine, I'm going with **plain HTML** (no build step, no toolchain — double-click to preview, deploys to Cloudflare Pages as-is; you can graduate to Astro later if you ever want components).

Now I'll build the actual site. It belongs in its own public repo, not the private planning repo — so I'm scaffolding it at `/Users/claudio1/dev/jdtogni-site` with real copy from the specs. Building it now.

Got it — you declined the file write, so I'll stop generating site files and check what you actually want before going further.

- **SSG** = Static Site Generator (explained above); given no node/npm here, **plain HTML** is the no-build path.
